antiPatterns.alternative: Only one FAB per page. If several persistent actions seem needed, identify which one truly must always be reachable and keep that as FAB. The others move to inline placements (Button, Button Icon in the header, Quicklink).
antiPatterns.reason: Material 3 expects a single persistent FAB. Multiple FABs compete for attention, the user can't tell which one is 'the' main action, and the metaphor of a single always-available action breaks.
antiPatterns.scenario: More than one FAB visible on the same page (e.g. filters + back-to-top + new content together).

antiPatterns.alternative: For per-item or per-section actions use Button, Button Icon or Quicklink inline. Reserve the FAB for page-level actions that must remain reachable through the whole scroll.
antiPatterns.reason: The FAB is designed to float over the scrollable content. Inline, it looks like an action on the single item nearby and loses its 'always present' role during scroll.
antiPatterns.scenario: Placing the FAB inline in the content (inside a card, between listing items, below a section title).

antiPatterns.alternative: Show the FAB only on pages that are actually scrollable beyond one viewport. On short pages, place the primary action inline in the content or in a sticky footer.
antiPatterns.reason: On short pages everything is already visible. The 'always accessible' metaphor adds no value and the FAB just covers content as visual noise.
antiPatterns.scenario: Putting a FAB on a short page that fits in 1 or 2 viewports.

antiPatterns.alternative: Add padding-bottom to the scrollable content equal to the FAB height plus the safe area, so the user can scroll past it. For very dense pages, consider a scroll-aware FAB that compresses or hides when the user reaches the bottom.
antiPatterns.reason: The FAB sits on top of the scroll: if the scrollable content has no extra padding-bottom, the bottom area is permanently hidden under the FAB.
antiPatterns.scenario: Letting the FAB cover critical content permanently (last item of a listing, inline CTA in a banner, important info in the page footer).

antiPatterns.alternative: On standard builds (Android, iOS) use the standard FAB family. On the Liquid Glass build use the Liquid Glass family. The consumer or builder selects the family based on the build target.
antiPatterns.reason: The standard FAB (Android / iOS) is an instance of the Button with two properties (os, Label). The Liquid Glass FAB is a separate family with Hierarchy (Primary, Secondary), no Pressed state, and a single size. Picking variants that belong to the wrong family breaks the platform consistency.
antiPatterns.scenario: Mixing the standard variants with the Liquid Glass variants on the wrong target build.

iOS / Android.conditionalLogic: Filter badge update: in the filter entry point pattern, the Notification Badge on the icon updates with the current count of applied filters. When the count returns to zero, the badge disappears (no badge at count = 0).
iOS / Android.copyAndTruncation: Label is optional (controlled by the Label property: yes/no). When present: short and single-line, no wrap (e.g. 'Filtri', 'Nuovo', 'Componi'). Typical examples are one or two short words. Long multi-word labels overflow the FAB shape and break the floating pill silhouette. When the action is universally readable from the icon alone (e.g. arrow-up for scroll-to-top), use Label=no for the icon-only square configuration.
iOS / Android.interactiveElements: Tap on the entire FAB area fires the consumer action (opens the filter bottom sheet, scrolls to top, or other persistent action). The FAB is an instance of the Button, so Pressed and Disabled visual feedback and the tap behaviour are delegated to the Button. In State=Disabled the FAB does not respond to tap. In the filter entry point pattern, the Notification Badge on the icon updates in real time with the count of applied filters.
iOS / Android.position: Floating overlay anchored to the bottom of the viewport with safe-area padding, typically over the navbar (bottom-right or bottom-centre). Never inline in the content. The scrollable content below must have enough padding-bottom to avoid permanently hiding critical content under the FAB.
iOS / Android.size: The FAB exposes two properties: os (android, ios) and Label (yes, no). Label=yes: pill shape with icon and short label. Label=no: icon-only square (44 × 44). Height 44 is at or above the iOS HIG 44pt minimum; on Android the effective hit area must be extended by 4dp total via container padding to meet the Material 48dp threshold.

commonPatterns.description:
Use the FAB (Floating Action Button) only for actions that must remain always accessible during the scroll of a long page. It is a single, persistent action floating over the scrollable content, one instance per page. Implementation note: the FAB is an instance of the Button, so all styling and state visuals (Default, Pressed, Disabled) are delegated to the Button. The FAB exposes only two own properties: os (android, ios) and Label (yes, no, when no the FAB is the icon-only square).

Common scenarios in the DS Cross-App:

• Filter entry point: floating over the navbar, opens the filter bottom sheet. Only this pattern uses a Notification Badge on the icon, to surface the count of applied filters.
• Scroll-to-top: appears past a scroll threshold, hides near the top. Typically icon-only (Label=no).
